Hi Elena / Marco,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I'm attaching our redlines to the MSA (Xeno_MSA_redlines_v3.docx). Two items we'd like to resolve before legal sign-off:

- Insurance offset / subrogation: Xeno asked if Redwood's indemnity obligations should be reduced by amounts paid under Xeno's insurance. We propose Redwood's indemnity remains primary but allow an insurance credit where Xeno's carrier pays defense costs directly to Redwood's insurer (see §8.3 in the attached redline).
- Defense control on IP claims: we can accept customer control for reputationally sensitive matters, provided we have the right to appoint and approve counsel for patent actions and to settle where Redwood bears financial responsibility.

Ben —

Thanks for the note and the redlines. Marco (our GC) is looped for legal details. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) We are comfortable with an insurance credit but not if it reduces Redwood's obligation to indemnify our users. In practice we want to be sure we can get timely defense and that any credit doesn't create a gap.
2) For defense control: Xeno's policy is to control defense for claims that could affect brand/reputation (customer data exposure, regulatory exposure). For pure IP patent assertions we are more flexible, but we need clear escalation paths and timeboxes.

Marco will follow up with proposed redline tweaks later today. A call tomorrow sounds good — procurement prefers mid-morning CET.

Cheers,

Elena — appreciate the quick reply. A few points Kimberly and I discussed internally and propose as compromise language:

- Cap: Redwood is willing to set indemnity cap tied to the applicable Order Form annual fees (e.g., 12 months' fees) for third-party IP infringement claims only; other indemnities (data/privacy) remain uncapped except for direct damages already limited under §9.
- Insurance offset: allow credit for amounts actually paid by Xeno's carrier but only to the extent such payments are for the same loss and subject to a mutual reconciliation process. This prevents premature offsetting.
- Defense control: Redwood to have initial right to assume defense for IP infringement claims; if Xeno asserts reputational/regulatory risk, Xeno may request control and Redwood won't unreasonably withhold approval for counsel, but settlement authority remains with the party bearing financial responsibility.

I'll drop a short draft clause below for your GC to react to; Kimberly will circulate a more formal redline shortly. If this sounds reasonable, shall we lock a 30-min slot tomorrow 09:30 CET?

--- draft (conceptual) ---
"For third-party claims alleging infringement of a third party's intellectual property, Redwood shall, at its option and expense, defend and indemnify Customer against such Claim; provided, however, that (a) Redwood's aggregate liability for indemnity obligations arising from such Claim shall not exceed the amounts set forth in the Order Form; (b) any amounts actually paid by Customer's insurer for the same Claim shall be credited against Redwood's obligations following reconciliation; and (c) Customer may assume defense where reasonably necessary to protect its reputation or regulatory compliance, provided any settlement that would impose an obligation on Redwood requires Redwood's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

Thanks — I'll confirm the CET call once I hear back from you.

Ben

Hi all —

Kimberly from legal here. I reviewed Ben's draft and attached a more formal redline (Redwood_defense_control_proposal.docx) with the following notes:

- Open-source / third-party model outputs: carved out from Redwood indemnity (we propose explicit language excluding claims arising solely from Customer's use or modification of open-source components and outputs generated by customer prompts unless Redwood materially modified those components).
- Willing to accept cap tied to Order Form fees for IP-only claims. We recommend a floor (e.g., at least $250k) for smaller initial pilots to ensure meaningful protection.
- Insurance setoff mechanics: require (i) contemporaneous notice to Redwood of any insurer payments, (ii) documentation of payment, and (iii) a 30-day reconciliation window before credits apply.
- Defense control mechanics: Redwood can assume defense within 30 days of notice; if Customer assumes defense, Redwood retains right to select outside counsel or approve counsel where Redwood pays, and Redwood approval on any settlement that binds Redwood is required.

I've included tracked changes and a proposed final paragraph for the clause. If Xeno is comfortable with these mechanics, legal can finalize for execution.

Attachment: Redwood_defense_control_proposal.docx (docx)

Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks for the redline. A few items from our side:

1) Defense control: for any claim that could result in regulatory notice or consumer-facing disclosure we must retain the right to lead and control the defense — reputation risk cannot be ceded to vendors. We can agree to Redwood-appointed counsel for highly technical patent suits, but Xeno must retain veto and final settlement authority for reputation-impacting matters.
2) Insurance credit: acceptable in principle but cannot reduce Redwood's primary obligation to make the customer whole for third-party claims. In other words, insurer payments should be treated as reimbursement that flows through reconciliation, not as an automatic unilateral offset.

I'll mark up Kimberly's doc and send tracked changes by EOD. Also please send sample certificates of insurance for Redwood's policy and the insurer contact for claims handling.
